flashcards.back: A relation formed from two relations by retaining tuple pairs that satisfy a matching condition.
It equates every same-named attribute, including names that may not represent the intended relationship.

flashcards.front: When does a LEFT OUTER JOIN preserve a row?
flashcards.back: Every left-side row remains; if there is no match, right-side attributes are NULL.

flashcards.front: How does MySQL emulate FULL OUTER JOIN in the deck?
flashcards.back: Combine a left outer join and a right outer join with UNION after aligning their projected columns.
A logical view exposes a query interface; a materialized view stores a result and may need refresh.
Autocommit is enabled by default, so each statement is committed unless an explicit transaction is opened.
CHECK tests a predicate over one tuple; a foreign key requires a matching key in another relation.

flashcards.front: What does ON DELETE CASCADE do?
flashcards.back: It automatically deletes matching referencing rows when the parent row is deleted.
It changes a physical access path and can reduce retrieval cost; it does not change query semantics or enforce uniqueness by itself.
GRANT assigns a privilege; REVOKE removes a previously assigned privilege.
A role groups privileges for a responsibility so access can be managed without repeated per-user grants.

homework.prompt: Run the Chapter 4 join examples on the University database. For each query, state which attributes form the intended relationship and whether unmatched rows should survive.
homework.rubric: Name the join type, predicate, preserved side, and one possible NULL result.

homework.prompt: Write a MySQL transaction that performs one valid update and one CHECK-violating update, then compare the database state after COMMIT and ROLLBACK.
homework.rubric: Record autocommit state, transaction boundary, failing statement, and final persisted rows.

homework.prompt: For a view that exposes only instructor ID, name, and department, decide whether INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE are unambiguous and explain why.
homework.rubric: Separate simple-view updates from updates that cannot be translated uniquely; cite the relevant page.

homework.prompt: Create an index on a selective University relation attribute and explain which query cost it may reduce without changing the returned relation.
homework.rubric: Identify the access path, selective predicate, and why the index is not an integrity constraint.

codeExercises.prompt: Write a GRANT SELECT on a restricted view, then list which base-table privileges are and are not implied by that grant.
